scope: UI history-read cancellation only; no Host protocol, model, tool, goal, or durable-history mutations
confirmed_defects: Superseded history generations invalidate results but previously left their HTTP reads running.
Explicit latest intent previously waited for an irrelevant pending bookmark page to settle.

live_observation.symptom: nginx chat stays at Loading history while activity projections advance
live_observation.journal: approximately 40 MB and over 53000 events at initial inspection
live_observation.profiling: WebKit main-thread WebSocket/microtask allocation and GC; Host also replayed journals

repair.generation_death: Abort only that session’s obsolete history reads before opening a fresh generation.
repair.latest_intent: Abort pending cold bookmark pagination and use its already validated tail.

red_before_fix.reason: No history AbortSignal was supplied; blocked obsolete reads could not be cancelled.

browsers.scenario: Virtual 100000-message paged journal; real Runtime, Conversation definitions and ChatView; blocked older read cancelled by latest intent.

regression.build_check: passed: production output matches the owned TypeScript source

full_run.failure: Unchanged strict HMR SSE lifecycle test asserted two async reloads after a fixed 30ms sleep; second reload was still at prefetch under concurrent test load.

limits: Synthetic read cancellation and pagination evidence does not establish the sole cause of the live nginx incident.
The actual running app has not loaded this patch; no post-deployment speed or memory improvement is claimed.
The 100000-event full restore uses the real Session/assembler boundary with opaque synthetic rows; browser rendering separately exercises real Chat definitions over the bounded tail.
No model API calls or Rust compilation were needed for this TypeScript-only change.
status: History cancellation repair and targeted regressions verified; running-app deployment deliberately not performed; sole live bottleneck attribution remains unproven.
